**Marks that lag, gates that bind**

Rating: underweight

Calder & Root reads the policy rate at 5.25% against cpi_now of 3.8% and concludes that real yields are restrictive enough to eventually pull spreads in and vindicate patient holders. We read the same pairing differently.¹ A restrictive real rate does not resolve fragility on its own; it merely determines how long illiquid structures can avoid marking to it. The one_year_return of +6.0% sits awkwardly beside a ytd_return of -3.5% and a drawdown of -3.0% — the kind of divergence that typically means the earlier print was carrying stale assumptions rather than genuine carry.

The reported_vs_public_gap of +1.0% is the tell we keep circling back to. Picture the chart: private marks drawn as a gently descending line, public proxies as a steeper one beneath it, the two converging only in the final quarter as the private line snaps downward to meet reality. That is not a coincidence of measurement; it is the structural lag our prior expects — valuation discretion smoothing losses until liquidity events force disclosure. Stonebeck Credit gating redemptions is precisely such an event, and secondary bids quoted well below stated marks tell us where the market, absent discretion, is already pricing the asset class. hy_spread_now_bps at 640bps confirms the public complex has repriced risk; the private complex has not yet been made to follow.

Calder & Root's "stay the course" reading treats the gap as noise that policy support will close from below. We think it is more likely closed from above, as marks fall toward secondary reality rather than secondary bids rising to meet marks. Should redemption gates prove isolated rather than symptomatic, and secondary liquidity normalize without further markdowns, our underweight would look overly defensive — that is the risk we accept in holding it. Until then, we would treat reported valuations with more skepticism than comfort, and urge prudent sizing ahead of further gating headlines.

¹ Restrictive policy resolves stress only for borrowers who can refinance into it; gated vehicles cannot.
